metadata.title: Municipal stormwater/MS4 deferred-maintenance -> private-property flooding, easement cost-shifting, and the utility-vs-city responsibility gap - a national governance-failure pattern
metadata.frame: A national, systemic pattern (NOT any single locality): ~7,250 MS4 systems under the Clean Water Act; deferred drain maintenance backs water onto private property; homeowners' remedies (inverse condemnation / nuisance) are real but often defeated by ownership-control + discretionary-vs-ministerial doctrines; utility easements (poles/vegetation) and municipal drainage duties overlap, creating a finger-pointing responsibility gap; HOA/resident land donations can shift maintenance cost to the public. The 'privatized benefit / public burden' + deferred-public-infrastructure motif that recurs across the corpus (Flint, ratepayer cost-shifting, the fiscal trap).
metadata.grade: statutes/EPA settlements/case law = FACT; the localities are ILLUSTRATIVE instances chosen for breadth across states; 'donate-to-block-a-road' and per-site utility/city disputes = graded/variable; no single jurisdiction is the subject.
metadata.honest_limits: MS4/CWA is enforced by EPA/states (water quality), not primarily by private flood plaintiffs; private flood claims run under state tort/takings law, where the city's OWNERSHIP/CONTROL of the specific drain and the design(discretionary)-vs-maintenance(ministerial) line frequently decide outcomes (San Diego pipe case; Shenson; AGCS v. Arlington).
metadata.method: EPA enforcement (Salt Lake County UT; West Haven CT); inverse-condemnation case law (Billie v. Channahon IL 2025; Lynch v. Venice FL 2024-25; AGCS v. Arlington VA); SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish; CALT/Iowa 'city liable for flooding'; Nolo (open-space donation).
metadata.water_utility_exemplar: American Water Works (AWK) is the water-side counterpart to NextEra/FPL on the power side: a national investor-owned utility whose acquire-municipal-systems + rate-hike model, ~$40B Essential Utilities merger, and Oct-2024 cyberattack make it the exemplar of privatized water infrastructure (privatized benefit / public burden), distinct from municipal MS4 stormwater but part of the same water-governance picture.

edges.notes: CWA Section 402(p) requires MS4 operators (~7,250 nationwide; Phase I >100k pop, Phase II <100k) to hold an NPDES permit + run a Stormwater Management Program (fact).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: EPA (or delegated state agency) enforces MS4 permits; civil penalties up to $25,000/violation/day; annual reporting - the program is water-QUALITY-framed but the maintenance obligations overlap flood conveyance (fact).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: CWA settlement: county failed to develop/implement its MS4 stormwater program 'to the maximum extent practicable' (fact) [1 of many localities].
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: Consent-decree modification requiring the city to 'immediately and continuously implement a preventative MAINTENANCE plan' - the direct answer to deferred maintenance (fact) [locality].
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: When deferred maintenance leaves drains clogged, water backs onto private property -> claims arise under STATE tort (negligence/nuisance) + inverse condemnation (5th Amendment takings). SCOTUS 2012 (Ark. Game & Fish): even temporary/recurring flooding can be a taking. Strict-liability in some states (e.g., CA constitution) (fact).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: Billie v. Village of Channahon (IL App, 2025): recurring-flooding inverse-condemnation/nuisance/trespass claims require proving the GOVERNMENT ACTION caused the water invasion - historic permit approvals alone insufficient (fact) [locality].
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: Lynch v. City of Venice (FL, 2024-25): homeowners sued for inverse condemnation/trespass/negligence over flooding that began Jan 2024 - active litigation over neglected drainage (fact) [locality].
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: AGCS Marine Ins. Co. v. Arlington County (VA): barred inverse-condemnation claims arising from municipal NEGLIGENCE - residents often can't prevail; the ownership/control + discretionary-design-vs-ministerial-maintenance doctrines defeat many claims (fact; the honest limit) [locality].
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: The finger-pointing seam: utilities hold easements with pole/VEGETATION-maintenance duties while the CITY owns drainage upkeep - overlapping corridors with split responsibility let each defer to the other (fact of the split; per-site disputes vary).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: NextEra Energy (parent of Florida Power & Light) - the largest US utility/renewables operator + a major datacenter-PPA supplier - holds pole/transmission easements nationwide with vegetation-management duties distinct from municipal drainage; the exemplar of the utility side of the gap (fact of role; specific local disputes graded).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: Documented mechanism: HOAs/residents donate strips/open-space to a municipality (conservation/open-space) - which can entrench land use AND shift mow/maintenance cost to the public. Eminent domain can override a pure 'blocking' donation (Shelton CT Constitution Blvd condemnation; Hays County TX donation-to-ENABLE) - so 'donate-to-block-a-road' is a real but graded/limited variant, not a guaranteed lock (fact + grade).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: Same 'privatized benefit / public burden' + deferred-public-infrastructure motif as the water-systems thread (Flint) - governance-failure where upkeep of shared infrastructure is quietly deferred onto residents (interpretation, labeled).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: FEMA flood-zone designation + climate/hurricane intensification compound deferred-maintenance flooding - a maturity-wall-like backlog of un-upkept drains meeting worsening storms (fact of exposure).
edges.source: #223 national systemic (EPA CWA/MS4 settlements; inverse-condemnation case law 2024-25; CALT/Iowa; SCOTUS 2012 Ark. Game & Fish)

edges.notes: American Water Works (AWK) = largest US regulated water/wastewater utility (~14M people, 14 states, 18 military installations). Growth model = ACQUIRE municipal systems (18 acquisitions in 2025) under state 'fair market value' laws + rate increases; $46-48B capex through 2035 (PFAS/lead lines). The water-side exemplar of the privatized-benefit/public-burden motif (fact of model).
edges.source: AWK addition (Food & Water Watch; Cornell/Pitt 2022; Stateline; CNBC 2024-10; AWK filings; SEJ)

edges.notes: ~$40B all-stock merger (close ~Q1 2027; merged entity keeps the American Water name, 17 states) - the TWO LARGEST US water corporations combining, further reducing competition; KY/OH clearances obtained (fact).
edges.source: AWK addition (Food & Water Watch; Cornell/Pitt 2022; Stateline; CNBC 2024-10; AWK filings; SEJ)

edges.notes: Privatization rate critique: post-privatization water rates rise ~3x inflation (~18% every other year, Food & Water Watch); a 2022 Cornell/Pitt study found private ownership drives higher prices + less affordability MORE than drought/aging infrastructure; NJ Haddonfield sewer bills +50% after acquisition; 'taxing through the tap'; PA Gov. Shapiro pushback + a bill to repeal the 2016 'fair market value' law. Balancing view: municipalities often sell because they can't fund EPA-compliance upgrades, and PUCs still approve rates (fact of studies/positions; magnitude graded).
edges.source: AWK addition (Food & Water Watch; Cornell/Pitt 2022; Stateline; CNBC 2024-10; AWK filings; SEJ)

edges.notes: Oct 3 2024 cyberattack forced AWK to shut its MyWater customer portal + suspend billing (no water/wastewater facility impact; language suggested ransomware) - part of a rising wave of attacks on US water infrastructure, some linked to Iran/Russia/China. The OT/critical-infrastructure threat overlay on the water sector (fact).
edges.source: AWK addition (Food & Water Watch; Cornell/Pitt 2022; Stateline; CNBC 2024-10; AWK filings; SEJ)
